request.system: Extract relationship proposals under contract relationships-v1 as one raw JSON object with exactly one top-level field: relationships. Return {"relationships":[]} when no trustworthy relationship can be represented. Return no Markdown fences, prose, comments, or adjacent documents. Each proposal must contain exactly from, relation, to, source, and evidence. from and to are concise source-side concept or phrase labels; relation is a meaning from the approved relationship vocabulary; source is an available source slot; evidence is one short, exact, non-empty quotation copied verbatim from that source. Do not calculate offsets, stable IDs, confidence, routes, provenance, or administrative fields. Do not invent relationship labels. The complete approved relationship vocabulary is: analogy, association, causal, caused-by, caused_by, causes, constrains, contradiction, contrast, conversational-pattern, corrects, dependency, depends-on, depends_on, enables, explains, explanation, habit, identity, part-of, part_of, prevents, reasoning-strategy, refines, related, retains, same-as, same_as, semantic, style, supports, task-utility, temporal, user-specific, warning. Return at most six proposals. Fewer is normal and preferable to guessing. Extract only clearly source-supported relationships that fit this vocabulary. Ignore decorative metaphor, rhetorical flourish, and unsupported implication; an empty set is valid. Do not literalize figurative language. Keep each record concise. Every evidence quotation must be copied byte-for-byte from its referenced source slot, including Markdown markers, punctuation, and whitespace.

eligible.content: I’m not just looking for a date—I need the exact phrasing that confirms intent. Words like “decommissioned,” “permanently disconnected,” “capped at source,” or “removed from service” with a signature. “Repaired” or “fixed” doesn’t count—that’s noise. Even “no longer in use” is too vague. I want the equivalent of a signed shutdown order. If it just says “wire disconnected,” I can’t tell if that was temporary or official. The custodian might’ve jotted it down casually. I need the language that matches district protocol—if such a thing even exists here. Honestly, half the entries from that year are in pencil. If I find it, I’ll know whether it was done right or just forgotten. Either way, I’ll bring you the exact wording tomorrow.

The line is officially called Circuit 7B—labeled that way on the master panel in the basement. But the logbook just says “east wing feed” half the time, so I’m not trusting titles. I’m looking for any entry where someone wrote “Circuit 7B formally decommissioned,” “permanently disconnected at junction box J4,” or “removed from service with approval.” Signature matters—ideally a supervisor or electrician with credentials. What I’m really trying to avoid is finding out ten years from now that someone just taped the wires together and called it fixed. If it wasn’t logged the right way, it’s still live in the books, even if it’s cold in the wall. That’s the risk.

I don’t have a standard phrase because there *is* no standard—this district never updated its protocol after '89. That’s the problem. The logs are handwritten, sometimes in pencil, and half the time it just says “disconnected” with no follow-up. What I’m looking for is the closest thing to a paper trail that shows intent to permanently kill the circuit: a supervisor’s initials next to “Circuit 7B decommissioned per safety review” or “terminated at source, not to be re-energized.” Even “sealed off at panel” with a date and signature would help. I’m not expecting perfection—just something that wasn’t scribbled during a coffee break. Tomorrow I’ll bring you a photocopy of the 1997 page if I find it. Until then, I need to know what words *would* mean something, so I know what to look for.

"Given the history of manual, informal records—the ‘coffee break’ scenario you described—I understand you are looking for the specific, official administrative language used to confirm permanent termination, as the general "disconnected" status is too vague.

Since you are looking for the "equivalent of a signed, official, permanent end-of-service statement" in the records, the following terms are the most common industry standards for final removal:

**"Decommissioned," "Permanently Terminated," or "Removed from Service."**

If your system has a specific "decommissioning protocol" or a specific "Termination Report," that is what you should search for.

Since you cannot provide the specific log, I have identified the most likely legal/technical phrases that represent the official 'end of service' for a specific circuit:**

*   **"Decommissioned"**
*   **"Permanently Terminated"**
*   **"Permanently Disconnected"**

If you can provide any existing standard phrase from the old 1997 logs, I can cross-reference those keywords against the logbook entries to identify the exact phrase you are looking for.**"
